digest.component_or_area: LLM prompt caching and cache breakpoint management in plan-review gates
propositions: Cache writes occur on every plan-review gate call but are never read across calls, incurring premium-rate billing for zero benefit because the marked prefix boundary sits after pass-specific content rather than at the shared plan prefix boundary.

The marked prefix embeds the plan text by design for within-run reuse, making content-addressed caching unable to reuse prefixes across different tickets, but the cache breakpoint does not align with the stable shared_plan_prefix boundary where within-run cross-pass reads could occur.

Single-step plan-review passes (finder, verifier, prerequisite-verifier, coach, ticket-digest) each generate one LLM call with a distinct system prompt; pydantic-ai's cache control marks only the last static system block, so three different pass-specific suffixes produce three different cache keys even when the leading shared_plan_prefix bytes are identical.

The diagnostic warn_if_cache_ineffective only fires when both write==0 AND read==0, missing the write-every-call-never-read shape that occurs when a pass writes thousands of tokens on every invocation and never reads them back.

Moving the cache breakpoint to the end of the byte-stable shared_plan_prefix (via a cache_prefix runner-seam knob that splits system_prompt into static prefix plus dynamic instruction remainder) enables the Pass-1 finder write to be read by Pass-2 verifiers within one run and by same-ticket re-reviews inside the TTL.
